subject: biology-1
question: A researcher adds a dye that is incorporated only into newly synthesized DNA to a culture of dividing cells, which spend most of their time in **interphase**, the growth and preparation stage that includes G1, S, and G2. During which phase of the **cell cycle** will the dye be taken up?

options.text: S phase, when DNA replication doubles the genetic material.
G1 phase, when the cell grows and prepares the machinery for DNA synthesis.
G2 phase, when the cell checks its replicated DNA before mitosis.
M phase, when the chromosomes are separated into daughter cells.

explanation: DNA replication happens only during S phase, the DNA-copying stage of interphase, so newly made DNA picks up the dye only there. G1 is a growth and preparation stage, G2 is the checkpoint before mitosis, and M phase separates chromosomes rather than copying DNA.
